# Homothetic pair contributions at the actual own-fiber centroid

Let \(K\subset\mathbb R^d\), \(d\ge1\), be a full-dimensional compact convex body with centroid zero and volume \(V>0\). Write \(\Gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d\), and let \(\Phi_d(r,s)\) be the symmetric-in-\(r,s\), degree-\(d\) paired-source lower bound proved in **candidate cd9374750b11bd94**. When \(r\le s\), it is

\[
\Phi_1(r,s)=r,
\qquad
\Phi_d(r,s)=
\begin{cases}
\left[rc_d+\dfrac{s-r}{d-1}(1-c_d)\right]^d,&r\le s\le dr,\\
r^d,&s\ge dr,
\end{cases}
\quad
c_d=(2\Gamma_d)^{1/d}\quad(d\ge2).
\tag{1}
\]

All depths and contributions below are absolute masses. Define the Minkowski gauge

\[
\gamma_K(x)=\inf\{t\ge0:x\in tK\}.
\]

It is finite, continuous, and positive away from zero because \(0\in\operatorname{int}K\). It need not be symmetric.

## 1. Exact homothetic containment and the displacement gauge

Suppose an actual convex body has homothetic fibers

\[
K_p=c_p+r_pK,\quad K_q=c_q+r_qK,\quad
K_j=c_j+r_jK,\qquad j=(p+q)/2\in\mathbb Z^n,
\]

with \(p\ne q\) and positive radii. Put

\[
\rho=\frac{r_p+r_q}{2},\qquad
m=\frac{c_p+c_q}{2},\qquad
\delta=r_j-\rho.
\]

Actual convexity gives

\[
m+\rho K\subseteq c_j+r_jK.
\tag{2}
\]

In particular \(r_j\ge\rho\) by volume comparison. More precisely, the support-function inequalities in (2) are

\[
u\cdot(m-c_j)\le\delta h_K(u)\quad\text{for every }u,
\]

so they are equivalent to the exact vector containment

\[
m-c_j\in\delta K.
\tag{3}
\]

For \(\delta=0\), this says \(m=c_j\). For \(\delta>0\), centroid support asymmetry \(-K\subseteq dK\), proved elementarily in the cited paired-source note, implies

\[
\theta:=\frac{\gamma_K(c_j-m)}{\rho}
\le \frac{d\delta}{\rho}.
\tag{4}
\]

The order of the two centroid differences in (3) and (4) matters.

## 2. Direct inner-copy transfer to the own centroid

For every ambient closed halfspace \(H\) containing \((j,c_j)\), the sum of its masses on the two endpoint fibers obeys

\[
\boxed{
|K_p\cap H_p|+|K_q\cap H_q|
\ge V(1-\theta)_+^d\,\Phi_d(r_p,r_q)
\ge V\left(1-\frac{d\delta}{\rho}\right)_+^d
       \Phi_d(r_p,r_q).
}
\tag{5}
\]

Here \(H_z=\{x:(z,x)\in H\}\), and \(a_+=\max\{a,0\}\).

For the proof, \(\theta=0\) is precisely the aligned-centroid paired theorem. If \(0<\theta<1\), put

\[
k=\frac{c_j-m}{\theta\rho}\in\partial K.
\]

Inside each endpoint fiber take the actual homothetic copy

\[
\widetilde K_i
=c_i+\theta r_i k+(1-\theta)r_iK
\subseteq c_i+r_iK,\qquad i=p,q.
\tag{6}
\]

The inclusion is the convexity relation \(\theta k+(1-\theta)K\subseteq K\). The centroids of these two copies average to

\[
m+\theta\rho k=c_j.
\]

Their scales are \((1-\theta)r_p,(1-\theta)r_q\), so the paired theorem at this common midpoint gives the first inequality of (5), using the exact degree-\(d\) homogeneity of \(\Phi_d\). This applies to every original cap, including purely base-normal caps and all closed supporting cases. When \(\theta\ge1\), the first asserted lower bound is zero and needs no degenerate-body argument. Equation (4) gives the second inequality.

Equivalently, the fixed-array source depth has concave \(d\)-th root on its midpoint Minkowski section \(E=m+\rho K\). For \(\theta<1\), the point \(c_j\) is the interpolation \((1-\theta)m+\theta(m+\rho k)\). Its depth root is at least \((1-\theta)\) times the root at \(m\), since the boundary depth is nonnegative. The inner-copy proof (6) makes this interpolation explicit and uses no additional regularity hypothesis.

The geometry of the zero case is exact: the paired source has zero depth at \(c_j\) if \(\theta\ge1\). Its two-source convex hull has section \(E\) at base \(j\). Outside \(E\), strict separation gives a containing cap of zero endpoint mass; on \(\partial E\), a supporting halfspace exposes supporting faces in both full-dimensional endpoint fibers, again of zero \(d\)-volume. This does **not** say that a zero conservative factor in (5) forces zero pair depth: \(d\delta/\rho\ge1\) need not imply \(\theta\ge1\).

## 3. A disjoint reflected-pair budget at one actual point

Fix an integer base \(j\), with actual fiber \(K_j=c_j+r_jK\). Select any finite family of pairwise disjoint pairs of positive fibers

\[
(p_\ell,q_\ell),\qquad p_\ell+q_\ell=2j,\qquad p_\ell\ne q_\ell.
\]

No endpoint is \(j\), and no endpoint is used twice. Let \(\rho_\ell,m_\ell,\delta_\ell,\theta_\ell\) be the quantities above for each pair. If \(A_\mu(y)\) denotes absolute depth in the **full original mixed source**, then

\[
\boxed{
A_\mu(j,c_j)\ge V\left[
\Gamma_d r_j^d+
\sum_\ell (1-\theta_\ell)_+^d
               \Phi_d(r_{p_\ell},r_{q_\ell})
\right].
}
\tag{7}
\]

Replacing each \(\theta_\ell\) by \(d(r_j-\rho_\ell)/\rho_\ell\) gives a radius-only lower certificate.

Indeed, every closed cap at the same point \((j,c_j)\) captures at least \(\Gamma_d r_j^dV\) from the own fiber by ordinary Grünbaum and at least the corresponding term (5) from each pair. These measures lie on disjoint integer fibers, so they can be added before taking the infimum over caps. Purely base-normal caps contain the whole own fiber and satisfy the pair bounds as well. Unpaired fibers contribute nonnegatively but are not assigned a mass budget in (7).

For a pair, write \(a=\rho^dV\) for its Brunn--Minkowski average volume and \(b=r_j^dV\) for the own volume. The conservative factor is also

\[
\left[(d+1)-d(b/a)^{1/d}\right]_+^d.
\tag{8}
\]

It is positive exactly when \(a>\Gamma_d b\). This is a criterion for this displacement certificate, not a classification of when an endpoint pair can contribute.

## 4. The coefficient \(d\) is necessary: actual simplex offsets

Let \(T=\{X_i\ge0,\ \sum_iX_i\le1\}\) be the standard \(d\)-simplex, let
\(g=(1/(d+1),\ldots,1/(d+1))\), and put

\[
K=T-g,\qquad v=-g.
\]

Thus \(v\) is a vertex of the centroid-zero simplex \(K\), and \(-v/d\) lies in its opposite facet. Fix \(\rho>0,\delta\ge0\), and form the actual convex body

\[
C_{\rho,\delta}
=\operatorname{conv}\left(
\{-1\}\times\rho K\ \cup\
\{0\}\times[-\delta v+(\rho+\delta)K]\ \cup\
\{1\}\times\rho K
\right).
\tag{9}
\]

Its three integer fibers are exactly the displayed ones. In fact
\(\rho K\subseteq-\delta v+(\rho+\delta)K\) by \(\delta v\in\delta K\), so mixing the two endpoints cannot enlarge the displayed middle fiber. The endpoint bases are exposed and retain their exact fibers. The hull is full-dimensional.

Here \(m=0\), \(c_j=-\delta v\), and

\[
\gamma_K(c_j)=d\delta,\qquad\theta=d\delta/\rho.
\tag{10}
\]

To verify (10), the inequalities of \(K\) are
\(x_i\ge-1/(d+1)\) and \(\sum_i x_i\le1/(d+1)\). Along the ray \(-v\), the last inequality is the first limiting inequality and gives \(\gamma_K(-v)=d\).

At \(\delta=\rho/d\), the actual middle centroid lies on the opposite facet of \(\rho K\). The cap

\[
\sum_i x_i\ge\frac{\rho}{d+1}
\tag{11}
\]

contains this centroid and has zero volume on both endpoint fibers. Therefore their paired-source depth is zero. Any proposed replacement of \(d\) by a smaller universal constant \(D<d\) in the second bound of (5) would give the strictly positive value
\(V(1-D/d)^d\Phi_d(\rho,\rho)\), a contradiction.

Thus \(d\) is optimal for a universal factor of the stated form, even with identical endpoint shapes, equal endpoint radii, an actual full-dimensional three-fiber body, and the candidate equal to the actual middle centroid. This zero-threshold argument does not claim that the full loss function is sharp at every positive \(\delta<\rho/d\).

An explicit cap branch illustrates that distinction. Set
\(a=(1-d\delta/\rho)/(d+1)\) for \(0\le\delta\le\rho/d\), and use the barycentric coordinate of the vertex \(v\). An ambient tilt can give one endpoint its zero-volume facet threshold and the other its threshold \(2a\). Their total mass is

\[
\rho^dV\,[1-(1-2a)^d],
\tag{12}
\]

since \(0\le2a\le1\). Its thresholds average to the barycentric coordinate \(a\) of the middle centroid, so it is one actual through-point cap. It tends to zero at (11); no assertion that it minimizes all directions is needed.

## 5. An exact shortfall of the certificate, with a safe alternative point

In (9), take \(d=3,\rho=1,\delta=1/5\). Then \(r_j=6/5\) and the exact gauge loss is \(\theta=3/5\). The right side of (7) is

\[
\Gamma_3V\left[(6/5)^3+2(2/5)^3\right]
=\frac{232}{125}\Gamma_3V.
\tag{13}
\]

The total mixed mass is \(M=(466/125)V\), so the three-fiber \(n=1\) target is

\[
\frac{\Gamma_3M}{2}=\frac{233}{125}\Gamma_3V.
\tag{14}
\]

Thus the proved own-centroid defect certificate falls short by exactly \(\Gamma_3V/125\), even though it accounts for all three source fibers.

This is not an original-depth counterexample. The old midpoint \((0,0)\) is an actual point of the middle fiber. The two aligned endpoint copies pay \(2\Gamma_3V\), already exceeding (14); the contained middle copy \(K\) pays another \(\Gamma_3V\). Hence the original body has an immediate all-cap certificate \(3\Gamma_3V\) at that alternative point. Equations (13)--(14) delimit the particular centroid-transfer bound, not the three-fiber theorem.

## 6. Relation to the archived centroid-surplus result

**candidate e4ccf81294305ade** proves a dominated-measure coupling for arbitrary source shapes, bounds the displacement of a weighted source centroid from the own centroid by volume surplus, and pays one own-fiber cap budget at the weighted source centroid. Those statements remain valid and are broader in shape.

The new input here is exact **homothetic** containment (3), followed by actual inner source copies (6). It transfers an already proved *paired endpoint* budget to the **actual own centroid**, and therefore allows the disjoint terms to be summed at one point as in (7). It does not assert a global inequality converting that sum into \(\Gamma_dM/2^n\).

The standard-library verifier **../assets/pk-nov6/computations/verify_homothetic_pair_centroid_defect.py** checks the exact simplex containment and gauges, inner-copy centroid identity, zero-mass supporting cap, the finite cap branch (12), and the rational shortfall (13)--(14). The proof does not depend on a numerical search.
